youtube.title: How if / else Works in Rust (and Why if 3 Fails) 🦀 | Rust Day 11 #Shorts

scenes.say: In JavaScript, if three just works. In Rust, it won't even compile.
scenes.captions: In JavaScript, if (3) just works. In Rust, it won't even compile.

scenes.heading: if, else if, else
scenes.say: Each condition is a true or false check. Four doesn't divide six, but three divides six, so this arm runs. Only the first true arm runs. Two also divides six, but it's never even checked.
scenes.captions: Each condition is a true or false check. 4 doesn't divide 6, but 3 divides 6, so this arm runs. Only the first true arm runs. 2 also divides 6, but it's never even checked.

scenes.heading: Run it
scenes.caption: divides by 3
scenes.say: Run it: divides by three. Just one line.

scenes.heading: First true arm wins
scenes.say: Rust checks the arms from top to bottom, and stops at the first match.
scenes.captions: Rust checks the arms from top to bottom, and stops at the first match.

scenes.heading: if gives a value
scenes.say: Remember yesterday: if is an expression, so you can store its value with let. Both arms must give the same type. cold is true, so temp is five.
scenes.captions: Remember yesterday: if is an expression, so you can store its value with let. Both arms must give the same type. cold is true, so temp is 5.

scenes.heading: Common mistake
scenes.say: Now the mistake from other languages: if number, where number is three.

scenes.heading: Expected bool
scenes.caption: expected bool, found integer
scenes.say: Mismatched types: expected bool, found integer. Rust never turns a number into true or false for you.
scenes.captions: Mismatched types: expected bool, found integer. Rust never turns a number into true or false for you.

scenes.heading: Say what you mean
scenes.say: Write what you mean instead: if number is not equal to zero. Now it's a real bool, and it compiles.
scenes.captions: Write what you mean instead: if number != 0. Now it's a real bool, and it compiles.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.say: Recap: conditions must be bools, only the first true arm runs, and if gives a value, with the same type in every arm.
